source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin AUS2-AUS3 campus publishes 19 MW of IT load across 242,000 square feet, a compliance-focused colocation site rather than an AI-scale power campus.

The two figures together work out to roughly 78 watts per square foot, which is enterprise colocation density rather than the density of a building wired for GPU training halls. The certification list, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, points the same direction: this is space built to satisfy auditors in financial services, healthcare and federal work. The site's suitability score of 62 is computed from only two inputs, published IT capacity and operator type, and the single input recorded as missing is announced expansion.

For AI specifically, the number that matters is the 19 MW, because power delivery sets the ceiling on how many accelerators a site can hold, not floor area. A campus at this scale can host meaningful inference or enterprise workloads and cannot host a frontier training cluster. The certifications also narrow the customer base, since regulated tenants tend to consume capacity in smaller, steadier blocks than AI training spend.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. It says nothing about how much of the 19 MW is actually available, how much headroom the electrical infrastructure has for higher rack densities, how the site is interconnected to the Texas grid, or whether CyrusOne intends to expand it. It describes one campus, so it supports no conclusion about Austin, about Texas supply, or about CyrusOne's portfolio as a whole.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
